title: David Fincher Says Brad Pitt Passed on His Scariest Film Idea
excerpt: David Fincher revealed that Brad Pitt was not interested in a particularly frightening film they discussed. The collaborators have also considered an animated project.
seo_title: David Fincher on Brad Pitt’s Rejected Horror Film Idea
seo_description: David Fincher discusses a frightening film idea Brad Pitt declined, a potential animated project and their reunion on Cliff Booth.
body_md:
David Fincher has revealed that a particularly frightening movie was among the projects he discussed with Brad Pitt during the years between their collaborations. According to a report published by The Playlist on November 25, 2026, the director addressed the proposal during an appearance on The Big Picture podcast. Pitt was not interested in making that film, but the two have considered other ideas, including a potential animated feature.

Their conversation comes as the filmmaker and actor have reunited for The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, which was written by Quentin Tarantino. Their previous movie together was The Curious Case of Benjamin Button in 2008.

## The frightening movie that did not happen

Fincher's comments indicate that the long gap between those films was not necessarily the result of a lack of opportunities to collaborate. The pair had discussed multiple possibilities before finding another project on which they could work together.

The frightening film was one such proposal. The available report does not provide a title, plot description, production history or detailed explanation of Pitt's decision. It would therefore be premature to identify the idea with any specific unproduced screenplay associated with the director.

A performer declining an individual project should also be distinguished from a broader professional disagreement. The subsequent reunion between Fincher and Pitt establishes that their working relationship continued beyond the abandoned proposal.

## A possible animated feature

The interview also raises the possibility of an animated movie. Fincher and Pitt have apparently been discussing such an idea, although the available report does not establish how far those conversations have progressed.

There is no confirmed title, production schedule, studio commitment or description of Pitt's potential role in the published summary. An animated collaboration should therefore be regarded as a possibility rather than a formally announced feature. Even whether the actor would participate as a performer or in another capacity remains unspecified.

The two ideas are interesting partly because they suggest different directions for a possible collaboration. One was a frightening film that did not move forward with Pitt; the other is a prospective animated project whose status is still unclear.

For now, The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth is the concrete reunion identified in the report. Fincher's remarks offer a glimpse of the ideas discussed during the intervening years, but further announcements would be needed before the animated project could be treated as an upcoming release.
